q: 1. Ties are load carrying members of a frame, which are subjected to ............
explain: In structural frames and trusses, a 'tie' is a member specifically designed to resist axial tensile forces.

q: 2. When a shaft is subjected to a twisting moment, every cross-section of the shaft will be under ............
explain: Torsion creates shear stress on the cross-sectional plane. Every point on the cross-section (except the center) experiences this stress.

q: 3. The shear stress at the centre of a circular shaft under torsion is ............
explain: From the torsion formula τ = (T·r)/J, when r = 0 (at the center), the shear stress τ is zero.

q: 4. The shear stress at the outermost fibres of a circular shaft under torsion is ............
explain: In a circular shaft, shear stress increases linearly with the radius. Therefore, it reaches its maximum value at the outermost fiber where r = R.

q: 5. When a shaft is subjected to torsion, the shear stress induced in the shaft varies from ............
options: minimum at the centre to maximum at the circumference
maximum at the centre to minimum at the circumference
zero at the centre to maximum at the circumference
maximum at the centre to zero at the circumference
explain: The shear stress distribution in a circular shaft is linear, starting from zero at the neutral axis (center) and reaching a maximum at the external surface (circumference).

q: 6. When a column is subjected to an eccentric load, the stress induced in the column will be ............
explain: An eccentric load acts as a combination of a direct axial load (causing direct stress) and a bending moment (causing bending stress).

q: 7. The limit of eccentricity for no tensile conditions for a column of circular section of diameter (d) is ............
explain: To ensure no tension at any point in a circular section, the load must fall within the middle quarter of the diameter, meaning the eccentricity e ≤ d/8.

q: 8. A column that fails due to direct stress, is called ............
explain: Short columns have low slenderness ratios and fail by material crushing (direct stress) rather than buckling.

q: 9. In a tensile test, when the material is stressed beyond elastic limit, the tensile strain ............ as compared to the stress.
explain: Beyond the elastic limit (in the plastic region), the material undergoes large deformations for very small increments in stress.

q: 10. The stress at which the extension of the material takes place more quickly as compared to the increase in load, is called ............
explain: At the yield point, a ductile material begins to 'flow,' resulting in significant extension without a proportional increase in load.

q: 11. The breaking stress is ............ the ultimate stress.
explain: In a nominal stress-strain curve for ductile materials, 'necking' occurs after the ultimate stress, causing the load (and nominal stress) to drop before breaking.

q: 12. The stress developed in the material without any permanent set is called ............
explain: The elastic limit is the maximum stress that can be applied to a material such that it returns to its original dimensions upon unloading.

q: 13. The ratio of the largest load in a test to the original cross-sectional area of the test piece is called ............
explain: Ultimate tensile strength (UTS) is defined as the maximum load reached during the test divided by the original area.

q: 14. The tensile test is carried on ............ materials.
explain: While many materials can be tested, the standard tensile test is most descriptive for ductile materials to observe yield and elongation.

q: 15. The compression test is carried on ............ materials.
explain: Brittle materials (concrete, cast iron) are weak in tension but strong in compression, making the compression test the primary method for determining their strength.

q: 16. A tensile test is performed on a mild steel round bar. Its diameter after fracture will ............
explain: Mild steel is ductile; before it breaks, it undergoes 'necking,' which is a localized reduction in the cross-sectional area.

q: 17. A tensile test is performed on a round bar. After fracture it has been found that the diameter remains approximately same at fracture. The material under test was ............
explain: Cast iron is a brittle material. It fails by sudden fracture with very little plastic deformation or necking, so the diameter remains nearly unchanged.

q: 18. Factor of safety is defined as the ratio of ............
explain: Factor of Safety = Failure Stress / Allowable (Working) Stress. For ductile materials, ultimate stress is often used as the failure reference.

q: 19. In compression test, the fracture in cast iron specimen would occur along ............
options: at right angles to the axis of specimen
explain: Brittle materials in compression often fail due to shear on an oblique plane (typically around 45 degrees) because they are weaker in shear than in pure compression.

q: 20. A column that fails primarily due to direct stress is called
explain: Short columns fail by crushing (direct compressive stress) rather than buckling.

q: 21. For keeping the stress wholly compressive, the load may be applied on a circular column anywhere within a concentric circle of diameter
explain: The kern of a solid circular section of diameter d is a concentric circle of diameter d/4.

q: 22. A truss is completely analyzed, when
options: the direct stress in all the members are found
all the external reactions components are determined
explain: A truss analysis is complete once the axial (direct) force/stress in every member has been determined.

q: 23. A tie is a member which
options: is subjected to axial compression only
is subjected to axial tension only
is subjected to moment tension only
is subjected to two equal and opposite forces
explain: A tie carries axial tension only, as opposed to a strut which carries compression.

q: 24. In simple bending theory, the assumption that plane section before bending remains plane after bending implies that
options: stress is proportional to strain at all sections
strain is proportional to the distance from the natural axis
stress is uniform in the cross-section
explain: The plane-sections assumption directly implies a linear strain distribution across the depth, proportional to distance from the neutral axis.

q: 25. If a beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive stress develops on
explain: For typical sagging (downward transverse load), the top fiber is in maximum compression.

q: 26. A member with a cross section of a mm² is subjected to a force of P N. It is L mm long and of Young's Modulus, E N/mm². The strain will be
explain: Strain = stress/E = (P/A)/E = P/AE, a dimensionless ratio (mm/mm).

q: 27. Find the elongation of a bar if c/s area of bar is A, length l, applied load p, modulus of elasticity of material is E
explain: Standard elongation formula: δ = PL/AE.

q: 28. If α is the coefficient of linear expansion, T is the rise in temperature then thermal stress is given by
explain: Thermal stress (fully restrained) = E·α·T.

q: 29. Thrust is induced in case of
explain: Thrust (axial force along the member) develops from the component of an inclined load along the member's axis.

q: 30. The diagram showing the variation of axial load along the span is called
explain: Axial load variation along a member's length is plotted as a thrust diagram.

q: 31. Dead load of a member is the
options: one that occurs due to dead body
one that comes all of a sudden
one that comes due to self weight of the object
explain: Dead load is the permanent self-weight of the structure/member itself.

q: 32. Stress in a beam due to simple bending, is
explain: Bending stress varies linearly (directly proportional) with distance from the neutral axis, σ = My/I.

q: 33. The maximum shear stress will always occur at
options: a fibre in the cross-section depending on configuration
explain: For a rectangular section max shear stress is at the neutral axis, but for other shapes (I, T, etc.) the maximum location depends on the section's geometry.

q: 34. In the case of H section the maximum shear stress will occur at
options: at the junction of web and flanges
explain: In H/I sections, shear stress peaks at the web-flange junction due to the sudden width change.

q: 35. If the stress produced by a prismatic bar is equal to the working stress, the area of the cross-section of the prismatic bar becomes
explain: As self-weight stress approaches the allowable working stress, the required area to carry additional load tends toward infinity.

q: 36. If all the dimensions of a bar are increased in the proportion n:1, the maximum stress produced in the prismatic bar by its own weight will increase in the ratio
explain: Self-weight stress scales linearly with the linear dimension scale factor n, giving a ratio of n:1.

q: 37. If magnitude and direction of a load does not change with respect to time, this type of load is called
explain: A load constant in magnitude and direction over time is a static load.

q: 38. The number of reaction components at a hinged end of a general loading is
explain: A hinge (pin) support provides two reaction components (horizontal and vertical) but no moment.

q: 39. If the elasticity of the material is zero then the material is said to be
explain: Zero elasticity means the material shows no elastic recovery — it deforms plastically.

q: 40. An orthotropic material has
options: different properties in three perpendicular directions
explain: Orthotropic materials have distinct material properties along three mutually perpendicular axes (e.g. wood).

q: 41. If a material has identical properties in all directions, it is said to be
explain: Isotropic means direction-independent material properties.

q: 42. An isotropic material has
explain: Isotropy is typically associated with homogeneous material composition throughout.

q: 43. A visco elastic material
explain: Viscoelastic materials exhibit both viscous and elastic behavior, meaning their stress-strain response depends on time/rate.

q: 44. A brittle material has
explain: Brittle materials fracture with minimal plastic deformation, i.e. a very little plastic zone.

q: 45. The compression test is commonly used for testing
explain: Brittle materials (like cast iron, concrete) are typically much stronger in compression, so compression tests are standard for them.

q: 46. A brittle material will
explain: Brittle materials fracture suddenly with little to no prior warning (no significant plastic deformation).

q: 47. The brittle materials have low toughness because they
options: undergo large plastic deformation before failure
undergo small plastic deformation before failure
undergo no plastic deformation before failure
explain: Low toughness in brittle materials results from very limited plastic deformation absorbing energy before fracture.

q: 48. A body having similar properties throughout its volume is said to be
explain: Homogeneity means identical properties at every point/volume of the body.

q: 49. The moment of inertia of an area will be least with respect to
explain: By the parallel axis theorem, moment of inertia about the centroidal (central) axis is always the minimum for any set of parallel axes.

q: 50. The square root of ratio of moment of inertia and cross section area of a member is known as
explain: Radius of gyration k = √(I/A) by definition.
